title: Data Protection: OCR's 1998 Act and Today's UK Law
intro: Catch up on the key A Level ideas. Complete four retrieval questions, work through the examples, then practise and explain your reasoning.

questions.prompt: Why must a server validate data sent by a browser?
questions.answer: Client-side checks can be bypassed, so authoritative checks belong on the server.
options: Client-side checks cannot be bypassed, so authoritative checks belong on the server.
There is not enough information to determine the result.
Client-side checks can be bypassed, so authoritative checks belong on the server.
questions.feedback: Model answer: Client-side checks can be bypassed, so authoritative checks belong on the server.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of an operating system's memory management?
questions.answer: Allocating and protecting memory for running programs.
options: There is not enough information to determine the result.
Allocating and protecting memory for running programs.
Allocating OR protecting memory for running programs.
questions.feedback: Model answer: Allocating and protecting memory for running programs.

questions.prompt: What is the worst-case order of binary search?
questions.answer: O(log n) on sorted random-access data.
options: O(log n) on sorted random-access data.
O(log n) on unsorted random-access data.
There is not enough information to determine the result.
questions.feedback: Model answer: O(log n) on sorted random-access data.

questions.prompt: Why does the TLS padlock not guarantee a site is honest?
questions.answer: Encryption in transit does not establish trustworthiness of operator.
options: Encryption in transit does always establish trustworthiness of operator.
There is not enough information to determine the result.
Encryption in transit does not establish trustworthiness of operator.
questions.feedback: Model answer: Encryption in transit does not establish trustworthiness of operator.

blocks.title: Key vocabulary
items: personal data — Information relating to an identified or identifiable living person.
data minimisation — Collect only data necessary for a specified purpose.
controller — Organisation deciding purposes and means of processing.
UK GDPR — Current UK data protection regulatory framework alongside DPA 2018.

blocks.title: OCR historic focus
blocks.text: DPA 1998 protected living people's personal data; OCR names this Act in 1.5.1.

blocks.title: Current framework
blocks.text: DPA 2018 and UK GDPR now form the core UK regime; later legislation amends it.

blocks.title: Apply principles
blocks.text: Purpose, minimisation, accuracy, security and lawful handling matter in a school. OCR 1.5.2 also asks for ethical judgement : monitoring and analysing personal data may be permitted in particular circumstances yet still introduce bias, unjustified intrusion or harmful automated decisions.

blocks.title: Give clear privacy notice
blocks.text: Under data minimisation, only collect what is needed for the stated function; avoid unnecessary personal identifiers, explain the purpose, set retention and secure any necessary records. A school also considers transparency and the rights of data subjects.
